chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Muhammad, from 'Abd Allah ibn Ishaq al-'Alawi, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from 'Aytham ibn Aslam al-Najashi, from Abi Basir, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about salat in furs, so he said:

“'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام was a man who felt cold intensely, and the furs of the Hijaz did not keep him warm because their tanning was with qaraz. So he would send to Iraq, and fur would be brought from your region, and he would wear it. Then when the time of salat came, he would cast it off, and he would also cast off the shirt that was next to it. He would be asked about that, and he would say: Indeed the people of Iraq deem it lawful to wear the hides of carrion, and they claim that its tanning is its slaughter-purification.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose validity is being discussed
key_terms.الْفَرْوِ: a fur garment brought from Iraq
key_terms.الْفِرَاءِ: furs or fur garments worn from animal skins
key_terms.الْقَمِيصَ: the shirt or inner garment next to the body
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: carrion, an animal not slaughtered according to sacred law
key_terms.دِبَاغَهَا: its tanning, the treatment of the hide
key_terms.ذَكَاتُهُ: its slaughter-purification, meaning what is claimed to render it lawful

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat in furs or garments made from tanned animal hides?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of performing salat while wearing furs and garments connected to animal hides. It reports that Imam 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام avoided praying in a fur from Iraq, and even removed the garment touching it, because of the view that some treated tanned hides of carrion as permissible.
